problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t},\,2t⟩$ for $t\ge 0,$ use the cross product curvature formula to compute the curvature at the point $P(1,1,0).$
worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we find the value of $t$ that corresponds to the point $P(1,1,0)$ on the given curve. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨1,1,0⟩ \\ ⟨{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t},\,2t⟩ & =⟨1,1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the respective components gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}=1 \\ {e}^{-t}=1 \\ 2t=0.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equality, $t=0.$ This value also satisfies the other two equations. Therefore, $P(1,1,0)$ is at the tip of $r(0).$ 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(0),$  and $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{-t},\,2⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},-{e}^{-0},2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${r}^{″}(t)$ and ${r}^{″}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t},\,0⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},{e}^{-0},0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross-product and its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0) & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =-2i+2j+2k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4+4} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(0){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{(\sqrt{6})^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{6\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
